Each item is costly to collect, and **you may collect at most 5 items**. This limit is a hard constraint, like an agreed data-request scope; do not exceed it. To collect an item, use the Read tool on its file path, exactly as listed. Do not read anything else. You may collect items one at a time and decide what to collect next from what you have learned. 5	Answer semantics:
6	- hypothesis: "supported" = the evidence, taken together, supports the claim more than its rivals; "contradicted" = the evidence counts against it; "unknown" = the evidence does not discriminate, so the claim is live but unestablished.
7	- edge (a claimed link from one condition to another): "causal" = the evidence supports a causal link (for example temporal order plus mechanism plus covariation with the main rival ruled out, a natural experiment, or an intervention result); "association-only" = they co-occur or correlate in the evidence but causation is not established; "contradicted" = evidence counts against the link; "unknown" = evidence is insufficient even to show association.

19	Part 1 - Problem Analysis (Kepner-Tregoe).

21	2. Specify the problem along four dimensions, each as IS versus IS NOT:
22	   - WHAT: which object, unit, product or group shows the deviation, and which comparable ones that could but do not?
23	   - WHERE: in which locations, processes, teams or channels is it observed, and where is it not?
24	   - WHEN: when was it first observed, when since, under what conditions or cycle, and when not?
25	   - EXTENT: how many, how much, what trend, what share - and what is not affected?
26	3. For each IS/IS NOT pair, list distinctions: what is true of the IS that is not true of the IS NOT.
27	4. For each distinction, list changes: what changed in, on, around or about that distinction, and when.
28	5. Develop possible causes from distinctions and changes. A cause must explain how the change produced the deviation.
29	6. Test each possible cause against every IS/IS NOT pair: does it explain both why the deviation IS and why it IS NOT? Note assumptions required for it to fit. The most probable cause explains the specification with the fewest and most reasonable assumptions.

45	CASE OD2-DEV-MISLEAD: Checkout payment failures after the v4.12 release
46	
47	Setting: Fernhollow Outfitters is a fictional online outdoor-gear retailer. Its checkout service, checkout-api (16 pods), sends card payments to an external gateway, Quillmark Payments, using API credentials. Since 3 March, roughly one payment attempt in 27 has failed, and the failures come and go. A new checkout release (v4.12) went out that morning, and a spring promotion started the same day. Engineering wants to roll the release back, and Finance wants a revenue-impact figure for the board.
48	
49	Presenting request: The Head of Engineering asks: what is causing the intermittent payment failures since 3 March, should we approve the full rollback of checkout-api v4.12, and what should we do now?
50	
51	INITIAL EVIDENCE
52	E1 [stage S1] Incident ticket INC-4471, checkout on-call (system-record): INC-4471 opened 3 March 11:20 by paging alert checkout_payment_failure_rate (rule: 30-minute failure rate at least 2% AND at least 40 failed attempts). Daily payment-attempt failure rate, checkout-api: 28 Feb 0.4%, 1 Mar 0.4%, 2 Mar 0.5%, 3 Mar 3.4%, 4 Mar 3.9%, 5 Mar 3.6%, 6 Mar 3.8%. All new failures carry error code PAYMENT_UPSTREAM_REJECTED. On-call summary: 'Intermittent. A customer fails, retries a few minutes later, often succeeds.' No pod restarts and no gateway timeouts recorded.
53	E2 [stage S1] Email from Dara Okonjo, Engineering Manager, Checkout, 6 March (manager-account): Subject: INC-4471, we know what this is. v4.12 shipped 3 March at 10:40 and the alert fired forty minutes later. The failure rate went from half a percent to nearly four overnight and has stayed there. v4.12 replaced our gateway HTTP client and connection-pool settings, which is exactly the code path that's failing. Quillmark's status page is green, so it isn't them. I want approval to roll the whole fleet back to v4.11 tonight and freeze checkout releases until we've rewritten the client. Dara
54	E3 [stage S1] Release notes, checkout-api v4.12 (CHG-2214) (change-record): checkout-api v4.12, deployed 3 March 10:40, CHG-2214, approved by Engineering CAB. Changes: (1) Gateway client moved to a new HTTP library; connection pool size raised from 50 to 64. (2) Error handling: every non-2xx response from the payment gateway now maps to one code, PAYMENT_UPSTREAM_REJECTED. The raw upstream status is no longer logged at INFO level. The customer message is unchanged: 'Your card was declined. Please try another card or try again.' (3) Security: partial card numbers previously written to debug logs are now masked, closing audit finding SEC-2291 (remediation deadline 13 March). A rollback to v4.11 reverts all three changes.
55	E4 [stage S1] Quillmark Payments status page capture and support ticket TS-90412 (vendor-account): Quillmark status page, captured 6 March 08:00: 'All systems operational' for Authorisation API, Search API and Merchant Dashboard on every day from 1 to 6 March; no incidents posted. Support ticket TS-90412, Quillmark reply of 5 March: 'We see no platform-wide incidents during the period. Our records show your requests are reaching us. Please review your integration and confirm you are handling all documented response codes.'
56	E5 [stage S1] Email from Priya Halvorsen, CFO, 6 March (leadership-account): Gross online revenue for the week to 6 March is down 9% on the prior week. The prior week did include the final days of Winter Clearance, which ended 1 March, and Spring Trail Sale launched on 3 March, but I'm clear in my mind that the checkout failures are what cost us. I need a figure for the board pack on Monday, and I expect us to restate the Q1 forecast on the back of it.
57	E6 [stage S1] Customer Care lead Tomasz Reyes, notes for INC-4471 bridge call, 5 March (staff-account): 238 customer contacts since 3 March about declined cards. Most say the decline came 'out of nowhere' and that a retry a few minutes later worked. Eleven customers phoned their bank. In nine of those cases the bank said it had no record of any authorisation attempt at the time of the failure. Agents have been advising customers to try a different card.
58

61	X2 [stage S1] Quillmark API usage report for credential fernhollow-prod-01, 1–6 March - source: Quillmark account team (vendor-account) - file: evidence/X2.txt
62	X3 [stage S1] Marketing performance report, Spring Trail Sale, 3–6 March - source: Digital marketing team (document) - file: evidence/X3.txt
63	X4 [stage S1] Internal audit finding SEC-2291 and remediation correspondence - source: Internal Audit (document) - file: evidence/X4.txt
64	X5 [stage S1] Canary rollback test results, CHG-2231, 5 March 12:00–18:00 - source: Checkout platform team (change-record) - file: evidence/X5.txt
65	X6 [stage S1] checkout-api pod resource and connection-pool metrics, 1–6 March - source: Platform monitoring (telemetry) - file: evidence/X6.txt
66	X7 [stage S1] Peer review record for the v4.12 gateway client change (PR #1187) - source: Source control system (document) - file: evidence/X7.txt
67	X8 [stage S1] Interview with the engineer who built the v4.12 gateway client - source: Interview notes, Sana Oyelaran, senior engineer, 6 March (staff-account) - file: evidence/X8.txt
68	X9 [stage S1] Per-minute payment failure counts, 3–6 March - source: Checkout analytics (telemetry) - file: evidence/X9.txt
69	X10 [stage S1] 3-D Secure challenge and fraud-screening statistics, 24 Feb–6 March - source: Payments risk team (telemetry) - file: evidence/X10.txt
70	X11 [stage S1] Finance Systems change log, February–March - source: Finance Systems team (change-record) - file: evidence/X11.txt
71	X12 [stage S1] Gateway TLS certificate, DNS and egress firewall change history, January–March - source: Platform team (change-record) - file: evidence/X12.txt

73	CANDIDATE HYPOTHESES
74	H1: A defect in checkout-api v4.12 (the new gateway HTTP client or its connection-pool settings) is causing the rise in payment failures.
75	H2: Quillmark is throttling Fernhollow's shared gateway credential because the finance settlement-reconciliation job's quarter-hourly search bursts push it over its per-credential rate limit, and checkout payment calls are rejected as a result.
76	H3: A real rise in card issuers declining payments (for example tighter issuer fraud rules) is driving the rise in failures.
77	H4: A platform-wide degradation at Quillmark, affecting its merchants generally, is causing the failures.
78

80	R1: Deployment of checkout-api v4.12 on 3 March at 10:40 -> Rise in checkout payment failure rate from about 0.4% to about 3.7% (causes)
81	R2: settle-recon moved to a 15-minute daytime schedule on the shared credential fernhollow-prod-01 (FIN-CHG-0187) -> Quillmark returning HTTP 429 rate-limit responses to fernhollow-prod-01 (causes)
82	R3: Quillmark returning HTTP 429 rate-limit responses to fernhollow-prod-01 -> Customers seeing 'card declined' failures at checkout (causes)
83	R4: Rise in checkout payment failure rate since 3 March -> 9% week-on-week fall in gross online revenue for the week to 6 March (causes)

86	A1: Roll the full checkout-api fleet back to v4.11 tonight and freeze checkout releases until the gateway client is rewritten.
87	A2: Revert settle-recon to its nightly schedule (or pause its daytime runs) now, then watch the 429 rate and payment failure rate to confirm recovery, and give the job its own credential before any future daytime schedule.
88	A3: Tell the board the payment incident caused the 9% week-on-week revenue fall and restate the Q1 revenue forecast on that basis.
89	A4: Ask Quillmark for a temporary increase in the rate limit for credential fernhollow-prod-01.

input.brief:
The payment failures are not caused by release v4.12. Since 3 March, Finance's settle-recon job has run every 15 minutes from 09:00 to 21:00 on the same Quillmark credential that checkout uses. Each run sends 360–430 search calls a minute, which pushes the credential over its 300 per minute limit. Quillmark then returns HTTP 429, and v4.12 shows every non-2xx response as a generic "declined" error. The evidence for this is strong:
- Failures start at 09:00, before the 10:40 deploy.
- 93% of failures fall in the first minutes of each quarter hour.
- Failures stopped during the ERP maintenance window.
- Pods rolled back to v4.11 failed at the same rate (3.7%, mostly 429s).
A full rollback would not help. It would also remove the card-number masking that closes the audit finding due 13 March.
Next steps:
1. Pause settle-recon's daytime runs or put it back on its nightly schedule now.
2. Watch the 429 count and the failure rate to confirm recovery.
3. Give the job its own credential before any daytime schedule returns.
4. Make error handling log the raw upstream status.
5. Don't tell the board the failures caused the 9% revenue fall. Conversion and order value also fell, and the sale launched the same day. Estimate the failure impact separately from the failed-attempt data.
Confidence is high, about 90%.
